<findings>
<finding task="0"><quote>The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software</quote><plan>## Decisions</plan><fix>The plan has no `## Review Focus` section; the header goes from Global Constraints straight to Decisions. Add the section between them with five lines. Candidates: a non-ASCII `compatibility` value; a `metadata` value YAML parses as a non-string (`version: 1.0`) in a real skill; an invocation split across a quoted path or a `$VAR` path in INSTALL.md; a headered script run inside an unrelated project; an installed llm-wiki copy that predates the headers. Pin each one with a test in the task whose code the person would see fail.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>R1.3: `compatibility` is "a string of 1–500 UTF-8 bytes after stripping".</plan><fix>This line sits under "Values copied verbatim from the spec" but changes "characters" to "UTF-8 bytes". Quote R1.3 exactly. If the byte cap is wanted, make it an owner decision and add a spec-amendment task (A12); do not silently restate the requirement.</fix></finding>
<finding task="3"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>if not (isinstance(compat, str) and 1 <= len(compat.strip().encode('utf-8')) <= COMPATIBILITY_CAP):</plan><fix>Measure `len(compat.strip())` in characters and change the message to "1-500 characters". Alternatively, keep bytes only after the amendment above is approved. Either way, add a test with a non-ASCII value at the edge so the chosen unit is pinned.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>**State test changes as +N deltas** against the suite, never absolute totals.</quote><plan>Expected: `45 passed` (+4).</plan><fix>Every RED/GREEN expectation (Tasks 3–12) and the Planning record ("1083 passed to 1121") state absolute totals. Restate each as a delta only, e.g. "Expected: the four new tests fail, everything else passes" and "+4 passed against the task's start".</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>A code step: the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer writes the body.</quote><plan>def bundled_license_violations(repo: Path, skills: list[str],
                               table: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]) -> list[str]:</plan><fix>The plan is far more than five times the spec's length, and most of the excess is full function bodies that the signatures and tests already determine. Examples: `_check_license`, `_check_value_shapes`, `_check_invocation_parity`, `bundled_license_violations`, `strict_violations`, `skill_body_warning`, `check_script_headers`, `_check_compatibility_names_uv`. Replace each with its signature, constants and spec values. Keep code only for the undetermined algorithms (PEP 723 regex, the optional-import walk, runner detection) and for exact copy.</fix></finding>
<finding task="6"><quote>A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone.</quote><plan>`FRONTMATTER_RE`, which Task 7 does not use and later code may.</plan><fix>This interface clause decides nothing. Drop it, or name the task that consumes `FRONTMATTER_RE`.</fix></finding>
<finding task="15"><quote>the full `build/` suite, plus every script suite whose script gained a header</quote><plan>no failure but the 4 `test_verify_citations.py` tests when the worktree lacks the gitignored `build/.scratch/`</plan><fix>Validation 1 requires the full suite to pass, but the plan accepts four failures. Either provision `build/.scratch/` (or run those four tests where it exists) so the suite passes, or bring the exclusion to the owner as a recorded decision.</fix></finding>
<finding task="15"><quote>`check_snippets.py skills/` (Tier 1)</quote><plan>Run `bash build/run_commit_lints.sh`: `commit lints passed`.</plan><fix>Validation 1 lists `check_provenance.py`, `check_snippets.py skills/` and the dependency-drift test by name. The plan never says the eight commit lints include them. Either state that they are among the eight, or add a command and expected output for each.</fix></finding>
<finding task="12"><quote>Here 3.X is the highest `requires-python` floor among the scripts that skill invokes.</quote><plan>'classification-codes': '3.11', 'describe-critique-methodology': '3.11',</plan><fix>The `build.py` scripts in `classification-codes` and `geographic-codes` keep their existing headers, whose `requires-python` floors the plan never records. Read those floors (for example `grep requires-python skills/*-codes/scripts/build.py`) and set `FLOORS` from them, or add a Planning-record fact confirming `>=3.11`.</fix></finding>
</findings>
